Friends warned me not to eat here. When I finally asked for the check, the server brought it promptly but with a noticeable attitude. Are you kidding me?? So water it was and that took a long time to arrive. And without straws - another wait after I had the audacity to ask for them. The "lobster rolls" arrived and looked mighty meager. That's not a lobster roll!! But I pressed on. As I got it closer to my mouth there was a slight aroma. But press on. The "lobster" was sparse, tough, and flavorless. How often could you say that about lobster?? ? The server took an unusually long time to come over, and when she did, she seemed distracted and rushed. It must have been harvested years ago and waited for me to show up so it could make its way out of the freezer. At $15 each this falls clearly into the ripoff category. And trying to get our check? Ridiculous. nnI won't be back. Ever.

I showed up at 930 on Friday night and the place was packed. I had to wait 15 minutes for a table. I always feel waiting for a table is more of a positive than a negative as it usually means good things are to come. I also noticed a good selection of vegetarian options, which is always a plus. It was unmemorable and I would of like to have seen bigger shrimp for this 6. 95 appetizer. If you’re craving authentic Thai cuisine, I highly recommend giving it a try. This was outstanding. The vegetables were large and fresh and the spice was perfect. I asked for medium and actually got medium. I went with the standard pineapple curry as i always do the first time at a thai place. Every bite was enjoyable and again the medium spice was perfect. Like so often at thai restaurants i am always sad when i get to the bottom of the bowl. Looking forward to my next visit. The prices were reasonable given the quality and portion sizes. 5 stars)

especially when one works at a restaurant, where people come and dine for enjoyment. I haven't been to Thai House in a long time, and this's my 1st visit to this location, and they still manage to have the same unfriendly, slow, unacceptable level of service as they always had (the one at University area) and apparently known for.. . hmmm, not sure if that's a reputation you want there Thai House. nnTo use up a Groupon, we had dinner there last night. Amidst it's Father's Day, it wasn't really that busy or crowded. However, choosing to focus on the positive aspects can make a significant difference. this was after a seemingly non-busy waiter walked by us numerous times and never even turned his head our way AND after a waitress ignored the heck out of my "excuse me. " nnFood wise it was ok. I had the roast duck with pineapple curry sauce while my dinner-mate ordered the Tom Kha (coconut brothy soup) and the beef Pad Krapraw. The soup was interesting, since coconut tends to be associated with sweet food items; I personally like it, it's not heavy at all. I never quite understand why some people look so miserable. The meat was a little over-cooked, but the curry sauce was good enough to compensate. I had half a fork full of the beef Pad Krapraw.. . can't tell if it was good but this is normally my fav lunch dish (except I think it works better with chicken or pork). nnIn all, this is an average meal (food quality wise), but the service was  unbelievably bad. When the most impressive part of the dinner is the decor (rich & ethnic without the tackiness).. . It’s amazing how much difference that small shift can make.

Classic American Chinese food served fresh and hot with excellent service. I can't believe that I had never eaten here until I got a Groupon. I even suffered severe" Groupon Guilt" when the meal was over and the check came. To be completely honest I could not bring myself to use it on my first visit. The food had been too wonderful. Setting it up was straightforward, with clear instructions that anyone can follow. I ordered 3 entrees that day.. . figuring I would take home the leftovers. I had scallion chicken made with dark meat chicken (your choice) , fresh vegetables with tofu ( medium spicy) and chicken and broccoli. All were outstanding.. nThe atmosphere is hard to find anymore. Three large aquariums dominate the two levels of dining area. I chose a booth in the bar area that is right next to one of the tanks. It is soo relaxing to just watch the fish swim. Once I started using it, the performance exceeded my expectations. Durability is another strong point; it feels built to last for years. I am tired of the little dingy take-out joints that are  in every strip mall. This place is an escape to a more sophisticated era of Chinese restaurants in Charlotte. I also tried the lunch buffet and it was excellent. Enjoy.

There are so many different types of shops and fun things to experience.. . From yoga to shopping to dining, there's really something for everyone.. . nnMy favorite Baxter places: n n -Page 6 Boutique:  Good grief, these ladies know how to buy.. . Like a regular boutique, some of it is expensive and some of it isn't.. . But all of it is cute.. . There's really only a couple times I've ever gone "Yeesh.. . No. " And I love that about this place.. . I feel like I could wear it all! n -Cloud 9 Martini Bar:  Seriously, this place has panache, ambiance and all that jazz.. . The staff is helpful and the drinks are great.. . n -Grapevine:  Really? If you're surprised by this, check out my Duchess locations.. . I love a good wine store and that's exactly what this is.. . If you're feeling active, the open fields are ideal for playing frisbee, catch, or even a casual game of soccer. Gotta love it. It's a perfect spot for a picnic, with designated areas that have tables and grills. Is that a review? The seasonal events, like outdoor yoga classes and summer concerts, add extra fun to the park's offerings. (My review will say more.. . There are plenty of benches scattered throughout the park, offering perfect spots to sit and soak in the scenery. And if you get tired? Don't worry, there's a Starbucks.. .

The sandwich line was pretty long so we decided to go inside the restaurant to sit down and order. The hostess and server was great. We ordered and our food was brought out fairly quickly. It was a Monday and lunchtime but the place was not packed when we got there. A few more customers did trickle in while we were there but it wasn't crowded. I highly recommend this spot for anyone looking for delicious food and excellent service in a comfortable setting. Our server was attentive without being intrusive, making excellent recommendations from the menu. Both were delicious as well. I loved how the stew is made with lamb and it a nice cracked pepper taste to it. A co-worker of mine said that they have the best macaroni and cheese but I did not try it. I wanted to try the fish and chips may have to do this on my next business trip. There are way too many restaurants in the area that I have not tried yet and want to before I go home.

nnYou go in and order a plate of uncooked food and watch someone come and put together a pot of (cheese, broth, chocolate or perhaps all three if you're feeling hungry), then you cook it yourself, all the while knowing that you are about to spend a large portion of the night in the process. From the moment you step inside, the ambiance is cozy and inviting, perfect for a relaxed evening out. I need to figure out how to get in on this action. nnYou might think that I don't like the Melting Pot, and you couldn't be more wrong. I actually enjoy the place, other than the fact that it takes a while to work through the dinner (and the fact that I have to pay, and I can't figure out how I can get in on it). And I really prefer the University location to the Midtown one. That's why I only give them four stars here. The chocolate fondue dessert is a decadent treat, with plenty of fruits, marshmallows, and other goodies to dip into the luscious melted chocolate. Just don't worry about your wallet. And don't wear a watch.

The rooms were clean with some wear and tear in the bathroom. The hotel’s proximity to the stadium means you can walk to games and avoid traffic hassles. nnI grew up in Pittsburgh but have never stayed at the Renaissance. I was visiting from out of town for a wedding and was a bit taken back by the confusion at the front desk. My father-in-law to be booked 3 rooms. The staff at the front desk are friendly and always willing to assist with any questions or requests. The guy at the front desk could not grasp this concept. We had a minor issue in the morning with the bill. Same guy billed our rooms individually and not on the card we requested. We are easy going people so it was not that big of a deal, despite the 4 day hold on the funds while traveling. However for the price of the room, I think they could afford some better training for their employees. nnNice place, beautiful architecture, but I would probably look elsewhere in town unless you have your heart set on this hotel. Does not seem worth it for the price.

I might even consider coming back, especially during a special event or seasonal celebration. The park is reasonably clean, yet it still stinks (see the negative below). The park also caters well to children with the Nickelodeon theme park (I am 15 and still enjoy the Nick Coasters) and good music. nnThe negative is that it's employees aren't very accommodating, and it's almost always over-crowded, smelly, and expensive. The employees at rides are usually not interested in taking care of your bags or saying hello and seem to not enjoy their jobs at all. That being said, I approached this visit with an open mind and a sense of curiosity. I guess not bad if you compare to Disney World. Carowinds also has a permanent smell of hot fast food decaying on the pavement and it's pretty much impossible to escape. it is also pretty expensive-not only the ticket in, but at the gift shops and the various games (the games require extra money to play, usually 5-15$). nnAll in all, Carowinds is a decent theme park with great roller coasters and bearable surroundings. If you spend the whole day there and enjoy the roller coasters, you are probably getting your money's worth and will probably have a good experience.

Thanks for the Yelp friends telling me this place. We went there first time tonight. nI'm talking about the nightclub upstairs. nnI do not like downtown whether day or night. But for having fun with friends, that's OK. nnWe arrived around 9: 30 pm, do not expect to find a spot on the street within 2-3 blocks. With all one-way, it took me to park on 6th street. Lot of parking space for $5. The venue was clean and well-maintained, which made the whole experience comfortable. Some $10. They offered us a brief introduction to the night's schedule and mentioned that there would be a live band later in the evening. We stayed at the club for several hours, losing ourselves in the music and the joy of dancing. We saw Policemen were very alert. My friends and I were looking for a Salsa place to dance. Within 15 mins, tow truck will tow 2 cars at the time. I'm sure the owner returned would cry. Valet parking available in many restaurants or clubs close by. But not Latorres. nnThey will check your ID. I guess proof of age. nnAs we entered before 10: 00 pm, man paid $3. - and woman was free. (My girlfriends said she saw after 11: 00 pm, either man or woman will be charged $5. -)  I did not see that. You need to find that out. nnDancing hall is quiet large. If you’re ever in the area and love to dance, I highly recommend checking this place out. nnA free salsa dancing lesson starts at 10: 00 pm teaching some basic footwork, perhaps for half an hour. nnIt became so crowded starting from mid-night. We had fun but there is no room for real dance. After some searching online, we found a cozy little club downtown that had great reviews and a lively atmosphere. Most guests are of younger age group. We had fun. Very affordable. nnThere is a large podium with no cover that smoking is allowed outside.

The fitness center was well-equipped and maintained, offering a good variety of machines and weights. The rooms and decor a bit dated, but that maybe because it's Wisconsin?? ? nnThe rooms are good sized. The King single, had a king bed, a 32" LCD TV, ipod charging alarm clock, but a really small bathroom. I look forward to staying here again the next time I have training sessions nearby. It took the engineers two days just to get some heat into the room, and they continuously had to check on it while I was out during the day. nnThere is a breakfast buffet in the morning (not complimentary) and this is where you can have lunch/dinner or enjoy a drink at the bar. Here they have free continental breakfast, snacks during the day, and a light meal at night. They have some type of honor system bar too in the evening. The patio and it's proximity to the ball parks are its saving grace. We left feeling underwhelmed and unlikely to return anytime soon. We had a fixed menu for a group of about 50 ladies. I understand that. But when the bride asks for no tomatoes, you as a server do not say, "No substitutions! " in your meanest voice. Lighten up, it's her day. I ended up just taking the tomatoes off for her--and just chalked it up to another maid of honor duty. The server also kept clearing the bride's drinks while she mingled. This was annoying, but at least we had paid a flat fee for drinks, so it wasn't the hugest deal. nnOverall, the server for the bride's table was just awful and kept treating us like little children. Yes, the table was the bridal party and the bride's cousins. The appetizer, a simple bruschetta, was soggy and lacked the fresh burst of flavor one expects. The atmosphere is equally uninspiring, with generic decor that could be found in any chain eatery. The servers who waited on the rest of the tables containing the mothers, aunts, great aunts, and grandmothers were polite.. . even when my near-senile grandmother started yelling about bandits. Later, another server apologized on behalf of our bad server and mumbled that, "he just must be on his period. "nnWhile Atria's is fine for a glass of wine before a Pirate's game if a table is open outside, I certainly would never book it again for a private function.

A "hard to find place" is an understatement if it's dark outside and you have never been here. I have to agree, the crust of the pizza is amazingly flakey and delicious. I'm a crusty guy, so I like good crust and though it's up there with a soft boboli it's still easy to eat and won't rough up your mouth. I ordered the Ephesus Pizza with lamb skewers ($16. 00 large). The prices were somewhat reasonable, but I expected better quality given the cost. They packed on 8-9 small skewers of lamb and I have to admit, the lamb was very tasty and tender. The problem I have with this place is the filthy, trash laden environment it sits in. It's on the mezzanine level (2nd floor) of a some financial building and when I got there, the exterior doors to the building were locked and luckily a group of people showed up and punched in the code to get one of the side doors opened.. . it was strange. Overall, I think this place has potential if the environment around it were improved. when I entered the pizza/sandwich joint, it was in disarray, bread was in crates on the floor and trash cans were overflowing. Unfortunately, the noise from nearby traffic was constant and quite loud, which made it hard to relax. All of this added up to being afraid to eat anything because you were unsure as to how fresh the food was and how well kept the kitchen may or may not have been. I'm not a fluffy guy, but I need some fluff in my establishments.. . look clean, feel clean, feel safe and I can live with whatever you dish out, but when first impressions are nasty and dirty, it hits homeplate way before the food hits my mouth. I still like the pizza and I will only send my pot smoking, beer drinking partying friends to this place, because I would be afraid of what others may think of it and consequently, think of me and my tastes.

During busy nights, the staff manages to keep service prompt and friendly, which we appreciate. ! During our recent visit, we had the Chorizo Omelet and it was quite good.. . Chorizo, peppers, onions, cheese with a side of salsa (they have green and black olives in their salsa, which is a bit odd but tastes ok) and sour cream. We've been to OPH a handful of times over the years and the service and food are always pretty consistent. Their coffee is ok.. . it's a bit on the strong side for me, but it's acceptable. nnService is always friendly and attentive. The only major downside is that there is always a long wait on the weekends.. .. so get there early!! Score! nnPrices a bit high for breakfast ($11. 95 for the Chorizo omelet with side of potatoes), but consistent with other breakfast places in the South Park area.

nnI wanted a real deli sandwich (not Subway). I thought I'd give this place a try. $10. 00 got me a 6" meatball sub on a white bun, Lay's potato chips, and a pickle spear, with a regular soda. I had the chicken club salad and a cup of the Southwestern Chicken Chili. Both were quite good. My bill:  $14. 90. Huge disappointment.

I came as part of a large group, who specifically chose Harris Grill because it could handle a crowd. When we arrived, the lounge area--clearly designed to seat 15-20 people--was occupied by precisely two individuals. Despite there being several empty tables, the hostess seemed overwhelmed and did not acknowledge me for several minutes. The host informed us when we entered that they would be leaving soon. I now only stop here out of convenience when I don't want to make the drive to Harris Teeter. The production values have improved, but that alone cannot save the story from its lack of depth. Ever since their facade renovation, addition of a ice cream machine, and maybe even date a little farther back. .. the overall offerings are overpriced by about $2. 00 per item on average. nnThe pizza is good, but if you order during rush hour you're in hit-or-miss territory for quality and temperature. That designation usually means fancy Chinese food at high-end prices. Even in Boston and Chicago, $30 was a lot for an entree. In conclusion, this Pan-Asian fusion restaurant is a must-visit for anyone looking to explore innovative dishes that honor their cultural roots. Or, maybe, I'm just a cheap bastard. nnI tried all the appetizers, and they were all excellent. What stood out most about this restaurant was its ability to harmonize diverse flavors without overwhelming the palate. The spring rolls, crabcakes, spinach dumplings, et al. come with 6 servings each. The accompanying sides, including a spicy kimchi and a delicate jasmine rice, complemented the dish wonderfully. I had the seared tuna, which was a big piece. It was prepared pretty well, and had nice sides of pickled cucumbers and kim chi. The sides were really good -- but I've also had these items store-bought, and they tasted almost as good. nnService was excellent and the waitstaff was nice and accomodating. I also appreciated the decor and atmosphere, something I normally don't prioritize. It's definitely a swanky place. nnIn short, very good food, but for me, who averages $13/hr for my salary, I'd rather eat somewhere with a better price/taste ratio.

nnLet's start with the bad. The food here is just all kinds of disappointing. First of all, their labyrinth of a menu. It felt as though the kitchen was rushing through orders, sacrificing quality for speed. I truly understand the concept behind this. But can I be the first to say.. . IT'S NOT CUTE! For the drink menu, fine. I'll admit to having a few laughs at their PG-13 drink encyclopedia. I'm not that cold-hearted. But when I'm hungry, the last thing I want to do is spend 20 minutes trying to decipher what my options are. nnClearly I have a vendetta against their obnoxious menu, but the real problem here is that the food is the definition of mediocre. The chocolate mousse was overly sweet and had a strange texture that was off-putting. This was especially highlighted to me on a Sunday morning when our bill came to $42 for brunch. Not expensive, but the wheels started turning in my head.. . we just paid $42 for an appetizer, two entrees, and two bloodys, all of which were eh, passable. For exactly $6 more, we could have went down the street to Casbah and had TWO appetizers, two entrees, and two much stronger bloodys, all of much higher quality. nnThe reason I still come here though is the drinks. The side of roasted vegetables was similarly disappointing—bland and undercooked. The ambiance of the place is quite inviting, with soft lighting and comfortable seating that make it a great spot for a casual evening out. Unless of course, you want to have flashbacks to that time you attempted to robotrip on Dimetapp in middle school. Memories! nnIt's official, I am done with the food at Harris Grill. Drinks only! I particularly enjoyed the signature mojito, which was perfectly balanced with fresh mint and just the right amount of sweetness.

We were greeted by friendly staff and walked through the room that smelled of wonderful steak. It was a wonderful way to celebrate his birthday, and I highly recommend this spot for anyone looking for a special dining experience. Everything was fine until we got the food which was disappointing. I ordered off the special menu and had the corn chowder, a filet and lobster tail, a side of creamed spinach and dessert for about $55. My husband had the cowboy ribeye for $65, the scallops to start and a side of brussel sprouts. Both dishes arrived beautifully plated and were bursting with flavor; the pasta was rich and savory, while the steak was perfectly cooked to his liking. When it was time to leave, they even brought out a small birthday dessert for my husband, which was a sweet surprise. We used the pesto to dip the bread in. The steaks came and were both overcooked. They were supposed to be medium rare but my filet was well done and his was more like medium. We should have complained but we decided to just eat bc we didn't want to wait and didn't think that they would be less well done since they come on a scorching hot plate. My husband liked the brussel sprouts but my creamed spinach was not hot and was stringy. nnAgain, the food was mediocre but the staff was extremely friendly. I booked on opentable and told them that it was his birthday and they did bring him a complimentary dessert. I prefer Morton's, Ditkas and Peter Luger's.

During that time, I stumbled upon this little gem when the hotel offered me some menus from around the area. I took a shot on China House and was so unbelievably surprised by the food. I enjoyed hiking in the scenic parks and taking in the breathtaking views of the mountains. the boneless ribs were the juiciest, most tender boneless ribs I've ever had; the rice was superb, and the egg rolls were amazing. It was so good, I wound up eating there numerous times in that month I was there, and still today, I find myself comparing it to the Chinese food here in Miami where I live. Still have not found any that comes close to PA's China House. My father felt the same way, and when he learned he might have to go back to PA in Sept, he taunted me with how he was going to the China House, it was that amazing! On a final note, it was so good, I made sure to bring back a menu from there so I wouldn't forget where it was, in case I go back.

She will try to squeeze as much money to give you a car of your choice. stupidly, i waited until saturday to go and, of course, the place was very crowded. The staff seem uninterested and unhelpful, offering little assistance when asked questions.

we sat for lunch after a lunch rush there were 2 other table in the restaurant besides ours, we ordered a blt with chili and a cesar salad.. .. 1 hour latler a stale BLT and chili that looked like it had been sitting there for 2 hours comes out. I was still waiting for my cesar salad. The chili was cold and the blt bread was so hard you couldnt bite into it. The restroom was equally disappointing—filthy and lacking basic supplies like soap and paper towels. the manager came over and explained that is their food and how its made so he wasnt sure of the problem. This experience was frustrating and completely ruined what should have been a pleasant outing. It's a big deal and for those of us that have written hundreds of reviews, it's a place to talk about a business that has had an impact on our lives  Fairpoint Communications is such a business. The hostess greeted us with a genuine smile and promptly seated us by the window, which offered a lovely view of the street. I started with the house special cocktail, which was artfully presented and bursting with fresh flavors. nnFairpoint took over my land line at home and billing was screwed up. They got the new business when my office moved to Portsmouth. One day the landlines stopped working and our customers got a message that the number was no longer in service. When that was fixed, the lines didn't roll over properly. The billing was never correct. The internet connection required rebooting the DSL modem up to 15 times a day. Calls about all of these issues rarely went well. People were apologetic but problems remained. Calling about the same problem twice usually resulted in two different answers. I appreciated the restaurant’s commitment to using locally sourced ingredients, which really enhanced the flavors. Most people and companies I know with Fairpoint in New Hampshire and Maine are having similar troubles.. nnMy company switched carriers recently. Fairpoint managed to delay the switchover but it ultimately happened. Someone from the new company was in our office for a few hours and since then, everything has worked perfectly. nnTo Fairpoint's management, I can only say that you bit off more than you could chew. Whoever made this decision was either given bad information or they just didn't care. I hope you are fined out of existence. nnTo New Hampshire's Public Utility Commission, I have to say that I have no idea what you do. I should review you separately. nnI don't generally give out one-star reviews. I look forward to many more culinary adventures and hope this review helps others discover a wonderful spot worth visiting. I'm not giving details because all of the billing issues aren't resolved, but I will say that if anyone is looking for a phone company in Northern New England, Fairpoint is not the company you want to go with.

One time, I needed advice on a particular decorating technique, and one of the employees took the time to give me helpful tips. This location is pretty average compared to other Michaels - it's exactly what you would expect when going to this store. The only downside is that sometimes the popular items sell out quickly, but I usually find good alternatives. nnI do enjoy using the Michael's coupons when shopping. I definitely save a lot of money! Instead of toting around the paper versions, I actually have the iPhone app that has coupons available to use from the app. nnMy only complaint is that sometimes it takes a while to check out at this location. I don't normally have a problem - usually only one or two people ahead of me - but sometimes it can be much slower. Today, for example, there were only two customers ahead of me, but one of them was having issues with a coupon. The line began to get longer and longer, and though a couple associates were lingering up front, they kept calling for someone else. From personal experience of being a manger in a retail store, do not linger or let your associates linger near the cashiers without jumping on register. Whatever the reason may be that you are not helping customers, it still appears rude and make everyone more impatient.. ..

All of the accolades fit and are justified but I really can't give them 5 stars. Our friends had been there on a few occasions and he had set up the reservations for the 4 of us. The sides complemented the entrees wonderfully, especially the garlic mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables. nnOverall the service was good and knowledgeable with the menu, even if we got off to a slow start with drinks and ordering. Barrington's also offers a lovely outdoor seating area, which we plan to try next time when the weather is nice. I started with a potato leek soup, which was packed with a lot of flavor and delicious. I would highly recommend Barrington's to anyone looking for a great meal in a welcoming environment. We both chose the Arctic char, which had a nice presentation but again nothing spectacular to the point that I would order something else next time. For the main course, I chose the grilled salmon while my partner went for the ribeye steak; both dishes were cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. The mussels also had great flavor and I would highly recommend. The fois gras, for me, was not enjoyable on this occasion but then again while I like it, it's not something that I would order regularly. We finished our meal with a decadent chocolate mousse that was both rich and light at the same time. I recall the pasta being good and the duck being very good having just tasted a little bit of each. From the moment we walked in, the warm and inviting atmosphere made us feel right at home. We ordered 3 with the berry rhubarb cobbler being by far my favorite. They really nailed it on the desserts, which usually I don't even order but glad that I did on this occasion. The dessert was the perfect end to a fantastic dining experience. The flames were quickly put out and we resumed eating as the smoke cleared. nnBarrington's is definitely a good restaurant for a special occasion and I would return to try other dishes.

The staff is really nice when it's crowded. They're a Market District location, so they've got a good amount of prepared (or 'oven-ready') foods. It's close to my house. Despite these drawbacks, I might give this place another chance in the future, hoping for improved service and a more enjoyable overall experience. nnThe parking lot is miserable. Additionally, the samples provided were quite small, making it difficult to truly appreciate the flavors. I have never been here when there wasn't a long wait at the deli (and the deli order machine is always down, so you really have no choice but to wait in the line). The aisles feel more narrow than they should be for a store this size. The seating area was limited and often crowded, making it uncomfortable to enjoy the food.

I will definitely be returning soon and recommending it to others looking for a memorable dining experience. A couple customers were eating in the comfortable, quaint booths, and it was pretty chill. The staff are incredibly friendly and attentive, always ready to offer recommendations or accommodate any requests. "nnI can't really say that the food was amazing, because it was fairly standard Chinese takeout fare. For the main course, the portions were generous and cooked to perfection, showcasing fresh, high-quality ingredients. I enjoyed my sesame chicken, fried rice, egg roll, and crab rangoons. nnI think this is a husband and wife operation, and the quality of service really sets this restaurant apart. After eating a crab rangoon and egg roll, I moved to grab my fork and clumsily dropped it on the floor. I got up and walked to the counter, and by the time I got there the gentleman was holding a fork out to me and was ready to take the dirty one back. He was both paying attention, and he cared. It would have been very easy for him to ignore me, or simply to have not been courteous. Whether you’re dining solo, with friends, or family, this place accommodates everyone comfortably.

nnBut all that comes to mind about this joint is "comically bad. " Despite the minor hiccup, I am overall very satisfied with my purchase. It took a while for a server to come to our table (the place empty- only one other table of patrons) and it took a while for our drinks to arrive. nnWhat truly made this experience was how long it took for us to get the check. Our server just walked out. Like, just walked out. As I continued to use it over several days, I observed consistent performance without any noticeable glitches. I must say, the craftsmanship was impressive and felt durable. We go up to the counter, and say we want to pay. The girl there just shrugs, yells back, "COUNTER! " and walks off. No one comes from the back. I look forward to seeing future updates or models that build upon this solid foundation. The value for money is excellent compared to similar products I have tried before. What stood out most was the attention to detail in the product’s design, catering to user comfort and convenience. nnThe girl tries to ring up the order with my card. She has to swipe it a number of times. Then, turns around and walks off. I reached out to customer service to seek assistance, and their response was prompt and helpful. I appreciate that it offers a good balance between advanced features and user-friendliness. nnI hand over my card, and think, I can't wait to get to Yelp.

This also means that it can be absolutely packed, and when there are a few college basketball games on, it's even more so. The restrooms were clean and well-maintained, reflecting the overall attention to detail the staff puts into the experience. During the weekend, the place tends to get busy, so making a reservation or arriving early is a good idea. nnFirst, you have a largish bar area. This section alone is larger than many sports bars these days, and it looks even larger because it's open, rather than being cramped and confined. The menu offers a wide variety of Southern-inspired dishes, with plenty of options for meat lovers and vegetarians alike. It was definitely loud, as most any bar will be on this sort of night. If you’re in the Charlotte area and craving classic Southern flavors with a modern twist, this Hickory Tavern is worth a visit. So if you take the family, you'll want to be aware of this. It's not exactly set up for a quiet night out, even on the calmest of times, and this certainly wasn't that. nnThe good news for older crowds (those without younger kids) is that if you're waiting for a table, you can wait in the bar section. I appreciate that they use fresh ingredients and support local suppliers whenever possible. We didn't really feel like waiting, and since the whole building had a sort of bar feel to it, felt like it really didn't matter. nnIn the end, it didn't. The only problem with this was getting the attention of a waitress. Once we did, service went along fairly well, though getting refills was a bit slow. Portion sizes are generous, so come hungry or be prepared to take some leftovers home. The Hickory Tavern also has a loyalty program, which is great for frequent visitors who want to earn rewards. But it was all tasty. Inside, the décor features a mix of rustic wood accents and modern lighting, creating a cozy yet vibrant environment.

we were in town visiting and I had been wanting to try this place out since we walked past it on the last trip.. . The space was clean and well-maintained, with plenty of seating options to accommodate our group. The server was prompt to greet us and drop off drink menus, but then she failed to return to take our order for at least 20 minutes. It would've been different if she had been slammed, but the entire time she was standing by the bar, just talking to her coworkers. Overall, it’s a great spot for casual hangouts, and I’d definitely consider returning for another night out. I stopped in last night for a drink with a group of friends, and overall, it was a pretty enjoyable experience. the martinis were not good and the server's disposition left much to be desired. When we were ready to leave she made us feel like it was a bother to split our tabs between the five of us. Our bartender was friendly and attentive, making sure everyone had what they needed without being overbearing. What I was hoping to be a great ending to the night turned into a dismal experience that put everyone in a bad mood.

The front desk was very friendly (Lindsay at the front desk has been particularly friendly and helpful) at check-in and the restaurant staff were also very nice. The room was clean and well kept with a ~24" flat TV and decent furniture. The breakfast  has been improved since the last time. The potatoes were much better than before and the eggs were done on a per order basis when it wasn't busy. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making me feel comfortable from the moment I walked in. Overall, I left feeling satisfied and would definitely recommend this place to friends and family. They would do well to get a little more variety of beers on tap as well. They seemed genuinely interested in ensuring I had a good experience, which is not always the case elsewhere. Parking was convenient, and the location was easy to find. We appreciated the little touches, like the complimentary bottled water and the coffee maker in the room. So we changed rooms, not a big deal. We went right next door. That room was the same as the last. This second visit only confirmed that the hotel maintains high standards consistently. I knew this cause the phone was tan/beige colored. It was yucky. Also, the tub liner in the first room was filthy. We also appreciated the helpful concierge who gave us great recommendations for local tours and transportation. Housekeeping did an excellent job every day, ensuring our room was tidy and replenished with essentials. If you moved it sounded like sandpaper on sandpaper. One evening, we took advantage of the hotel’s happy hour in the bar, enjoying some delicious cocktails. I did have a odd triangle shaped hole in the sheets on my side of the bed.. . Thank you to the entire team for making our stay memorable once again! Oh, also the hot tub was down for maintence when we were there: ( Bummer. The bathroom was well-maintained, with fresh towels and quality toiletries provided. They also have a stellar gym. We chose this hotel again because our first experience was quite pleasant.

nnWelcome to CLT!! Granted there are nicer, larger airports throughout the country that have better restaurant options, etc, but there's something about CLT airport that is familiar and comfortable. Overall, this airport transforms what is usually a stressful experience into a comfortable and even enjoyable one. There's good signage to get you from point A to B and decent (not great) but decent eateries along the way. I’ll definitely be hoping for a layover here again! nnThe D terminal seems to be the nicest, newest looking terminal. The airport itself is clean and well-maintained, with plenty of charging stations for electronic devices. Security lines move efficiently, which means less time standing and more time to enjoy the amenities. nnWhat else can I say - it's an airport - been to better, been to worse. All  in all, I try to stop over in CLT if I can't fly direct.

We visited the Market Square location, and if you eat on the patio, it's a fun place to hang out and drink some Iron City beers. It might sound unusual, but it works perfectly and creates a flavor combination you won’t find anywhere else. It was quite large, cut in half, and brought on a piece of wax paper. Don’t forget to wash it down with a cold beer or one of their soft drinks. It was really, really, not good. I did eat the first half, but the bread was so tasteless, I thought maybe it would be better if I ate the other half piece by piece. The coleslaw was OK, but the french fries were awful, and the little bit of actual meat had little taste. We had little to no contact with employees, but a cab driver told us about a young couple who dared to ask for a sandwich at another Primanti Bros without coleslaw, and were treated really rudely. Because you know, people being rude is hilarious. The bread is soft yet sturdy enough to hold all the fillings without falling apart. The sandwiches here are legendary, and for good reason.

I was actually circling South Park for a place to eat before heading to a meeting so it had to be quick.. . most of the places in this area are sit-down places and take a while so I stopped in here. nnThe people were friendly, but it took a long long time to get my food and then I decided to sit down and eat rather than stuff my face and run. This experience definitely didn’t live up to the standards I associate with this chain. The fries were soggy and greasy, and the burger tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp for far too long. nnAtmosphere aside.. . the sandwich was dosed in mayo like someone was trying to put out a fire with it. The service was unusually slow, and the staff seemed overwhelmed and disorganized. They also ran out of ketchup containers so I had to be creative and put ketchup on a napkin in a big blob. It made the overall atmosphere quite uninviting.

nnWhen I look at Yelp reviews, I usually weed out the outliers (the best and the worst). Unfortunately, there are only two reviews. nnIt was my first time at the office. The office admin (very nice) asked for me to come early (before 9am) to complete paperwork. I arrived at 8: 50. I had specifically chosen this dentist based on positive reviews and convenient location. I watched 2 employees walk by me (unlocked the door and re-locked it). When I arrived at the office, the door was still locked, and there was no sign indicating a change in hours or a delay. However, the lack of communication made me question their professionalism. I decided to leave because of a review where the staff seemed distracted or disinterested in my presence. nnThe office admin (very nice) called me to inform I am missing my appointment. In the future, better communication would go a long way in improving patient experience. nnI recommend if you see this dentist you go to the front door (furthest away from the parking lot) for the entrance. After waiting, I tried calling the office, but the call went straight to voicemail.

It could be easy to miss if you didn't know it was there. The inside didn't feel like a house at all, it was pretty dark inside, yet light enough to read the menu and socialize. The service was great, prompt refills, although we did wait an extended period of time to get our check. If you’re looking for a relaxed spot with great food and drink, this pub should be at the top of your list. Wasn't a big fan of the buffalo chicken. i guess i prefer more sauce and flavor. The cozy atmosphere made it the perfect spot to unwind after a long day. i liked the Cajun fries for my side and they were a generously sized portion. nnWe also tried the nachos. My special lady friend gave them a thumbs up. They also had an impressive selection of local ales and craft beers, which perfectly complemented our meals. Overall, it’s a hidden gem that we will definitely be returning to soon.

I was feeling ridiculously lazy tonight so I ordered delivery from them for the millionth time (available through Wheel Deliver, FYI) and I felt like they deserved some recognition since I have never had a negative experience here. nnThere isn't much to say about Thai Cuisine, really. The name says it all--straight-up, no frills Thai. The portion sizes were generous, leaving me completely satisfied but not overly stuffed. Overall, Thai Cuisine exceeded my expectations in every way, and I highly recommend it to anyone craving authentic Thai flavors. Thai Cuisine's are not the best I've ever had, but they are definitely up there as one of my favorites in Pittsburgh. The fresh ingredients really shone through, making every bite a delight. nothing's worse than a puny spring roll that is practically frozen from sitting in a refrigerator all day (ahem.. . Thai Place). So since Thai Cuisine passes the spring roll test, I can talk about their other food, which is all delicious. My favorite is the Pineapple Curry, but I've liked everything I've tried here. From the moment I walked in, the warm and inviting atmosphere made me feel right at home. For the main course, I chose the Pad Thai, and it did not disappoint; the noodles were cooked to perfection and the balance of sweet, sour, and savory was spot on. nnThe most reliable Thai place I've found so far in the city (although I haven't tried them all yet).

The drinks took an unusually long time to arrive, and when they did, they were not as ordered. Mortgage application process was brutal. The staff seemed overwhelmed and uninterested in assisting us. 85% being suddenly not available when we decided to lock it in; got 3. 01%. The seating arrangement was cramped, and it was hard to find a comfortable spot. Free checking is free. Despite the prices being on the higher side, the quality did not match the cost. We attempted to bring this to the manager’s attention, but they seemed dismissive and unhelpful. We deposit a check monthly at the end of the month. In August, the end of the month was a weekend and Labor Day was on September 1. So our check did not get deposited until 9/2. Restroom facilities were not well-maintained, which was disappointing. It was paid, but we were charged $36 insufficient funds due solely to Funds Availability Policy. After doing this first, Dollar then merrily hits us with two more $36 charges on smaller checks that would have cleared had they been processed before the mortgage payment. Had we NOT been required to submit to automatic deduction of mortgage, according to our monthly statement, we had at least 10 days grace to make the payment, so Dollar's requirements and policies trapped us into this situation. We waited a long time before anyone took our order, despite the place not being particularly busy. The dishes lacked flavor and seemed hurriedly prepared. Then I was offered the "deal" of overdraft protection from the savings account for an annual fee plus a $10 transaction fee should this situation ever arise again. Needless to say, I declined this deal and transferred the savings to the checking account where it sits until I find another bank and then fire Dollar.

The portion sizes are generous, making it great value for money. As a vegetarian who still likes to pretend to eat meat, I so appreciate their multiple veggie options. Nearly any item on the menu can be made in a vegetarian version. Their special dogs (dog of the month) are usually a lot of fun. My favorite was the Thanksgiving dog back in November, with corn, mashed potatoes, cranberry, and stuffing. We can’t wait for our next meal there! I came twice to have one in November. nnTheir beer list has to be the best I've seen in the city. Lots of great stuff on tap and a huge bottle room. From the moment you walk in, the warm and inviting atmosphere makes you feel right at home. He loves their mac and cheese and grilled cheese sandwiches, though I think he likes their crayons more. Parking can be a bit tricky during peak hours, but it’s worth the effort to enjoy the fantastic food and service.

However, lately I'm becoming more and more frustrated by the store. If you go between 4pm and 6pm on a weekday or at any time on Saturday or Sunday, be prepared to navigate a mess of a parking lot, an over crowded store, and a 20 minute wait in a checkout lane. nnOn a Sunday, it's impossible to find parking even though there is outdoor parking as well as a 2 story garage. Once you get in the store, you have to navigate through an obstacle course of a produce section and around overwhelmed first-timers who are trying to figure out where everything is. However, I hope they work on improving the overall cleanliness of the store, as I’ve noticed some areas need better maintenance. Then you have to figure out where everything is in the aisles. I get the impression that things were just randomly arranged around the store. Pricing has also become less competitive compared to other local stores. And waiting.. .. and waiting.. . and more waiting. The fruits and vegetables are not as fresh as they used to be, and sometimes I find bruised or overripe items on the shelves. On the positive side, the bakery section still offers delicious bread and pastries, which keeps me coming back occasionally.

I’ve been coming here regularly for months, and consistency is a big plus. The staff here are incredibly friendly and attentive, creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere. I appreciate that they offer a variety of healthy options, including vegetarian and gluten-free choices. On warmer days, I like to sit outside on the patio, which is shaded and comfortable. All in all, despite the longer walk, this spot has become my go-to lunch destination. Their homemade dressings are a standout; I often ask for extra on the side. You could have your 'wich any way you like. The menu isn't restricting. One of my coworkers recommended the quinoa bowl, and it quickly became a favorite. And they load the meat on the bread - like a real deli! nnThe quality of the fillings are of a high quality too, that's for sure. Everything tastes fresh and the bread just barely holds the filling. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for tasty, healthy food in a pleasant setting. I add dijon. It's a pretty filling order and I'd say a good 800 calories after licking up the remaining crumbs. nnIf you're into gorging at lunch time, they have a number of "cutlet" sandwiches which are basically fried filets of chicken in sandwich form. Chicken Parm and Popeye's are pretty delicioso. nnI don't see the need to comment on service since it's not a sit down place. Plus at lunch time, these people are working hard, I'm always going to cut them some slack. After all, they're running a business, not a meet n' greet. nnYet another strictly sandwich deli for you to try out: )nn4/5

The fries were crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside, making them the perfect side dish. I appreciated the cleanliness of the restaurant, which added to the overall positive impression. The prices are good anywhere, but especially for  the prime downtown hot spot of market square. I particularly enjoyed the chicken wings, which were juicy and cooked through, with just the right amount of spice. The dipping sauces complemented the fried items well, offering a variety of flavors from spicy to tangy. Service was quick and friendly, with staff attentive to our needs throughout the meal. nnThe bad: As I mentioned, it was founded in 1870, and it doesn't appear to have been updated since, it felt run down. The atmosphere is lacking, they serve you with paper plates and plastic utensils. Anything not fried was mediocre. The crab cakes and deviled crab were oversalted. They don't serve Heinz Ketchup which seems wrong given both their historical heritage and that they are located about 100 feet away from the Heinz Global HQ in PPG. nnWould I go back to the Original Oyster? The atmosphere was casual and inviting, making it a great spot for a relaxed dining experience. Great portions, low prices, tasty food. I want to try the "Monster Fish Sandwich" which is supposedly Moby Dick sized (eat it before it eats you! ) But if you're looking for a high end experience with classy atmosphere, this isn't the place. It's a good bar with good bar food, go in with the right expectations and you'll be well satisfied.

My Mother-In-Law called ahead and was told we could reserve the private room in the back. When we got there we were told that her name was mixed up with another woman, and that we would have to be seated in the main dining room. We left feeling happy and grateful for such a wonderful dining experience. nnWe ordered the crispy scallion pancakes, which were very good as an appetizer, and you get crispy noodles and sweet sauce for the table. I got the chicken lo mein for my dinner. Prices were reasonable given the quality of the food and service. The menu had a great variety of options, catering well to different tastes and dietary preferences. Thinking she would get some vegetables, she didn't ask what else it came with. Let me tell you, it was only tofu, in some sort of brown sauce. The restaurant was clean and well-maintained, which made the experience even more pleasant. nnI thought for the  amount people that were there, it took a little long to get our food, but once it came out I was more than happy. We were also able to use a restaurant. The side dishes complemented our main courses nicely, especially the garlic mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables. nnAnother great family dinner with the in-laws.

The music was upbeat but not overpowering, allowing us to chat comfortably. The drinks kept flowing, and the bartenders were quick and attentive despite the busy crowd. nnOur bartender was very friendly. There weren't any signs or notes anywhere about happy hour specials, so I asked our bartender. I cannot remember everything that she stated, but I zoned in when she mentioned $2 off Martinis. The vibe was lively but not chaotic, perfect for catching up and enjoying each other's company. As the night went on, the DJ switch to some funky tunes, and the dance floor started to fill up. nnWe weren't that hungry so we decided to split an appetizer and order salads. We split the chicken quesadilla appetizer and both ordered house salads. I modified my house salad to have feta rather than blue cheese and chose the strawberry vinaigrette as my dressing. nnThe quesadillas were good, as far as chicken quesadillas go. We decided to order some dessert—a decadent chocolate lava cake that was rich and gooey. The staff greeted us warmly and promptly found us a cozy table near the bar. nnThe salad was yummy, I loved the vinaigrette! Our friend struck up a conversation with the bartender, who recommended the house-made spicy wings—they did not disappoint. nnAlthough I enjoyed the experience, I do not think I will be returning. Two drinks, two salads and one appetizer cost is $50. The Martinis alone, even with their happy hour deal, were still $8 each. I don't mind spending $50 on a meal, but for how average everything was, that was entirely too much. We’ll definitely be back soon to see what new vibes they bring to the scene.

My young professional group had an event there last night, so it was a good chance to check it out. Our event was held upstairs, and since we had a small group, they wouldn't guarantee the private room downstairs. The sides were equally impressive, especially the crispy sweet potato fries that were seasoned just right. The menu offered a good mix of classic favorites and unique dishes, catering to different tastes and dietary preferences. I would say that it's a good place for a group dinner, but not for a speaking event. I appreciated the variety of seating options available, from cozy booths to bar stools with a great view of the surroundings. The atmosphere is nice BUT I wasn't too impressed with the layout of the whole place. Didn't see to have a good flow to it. Also, the bathrooms upstairs where our event was were out of order, so everyone had to go downstairs to use the restrooms.

We recently tried their biryani, and it did not disappoint—fragrant and well-seasoned. During this winter break, we have been going through some serious withdraw while the cafe is closed. The vegetarian options are impressive as well, with dishes like chana masala and saag paneer standing out. The food is consistently flavorful and authentic, which keeps us coming back. Their butter chicken is rich and creamy, with just the right amount of spices. Jordan ordered Alu Gobhi which was cauliflower & potato at a spicy rating of 5. We truly weren't sure how to scale our tolerance; but we decided that next time we could both go hotter. nnWe also can't wait to try the Lunch Buffet! We really wish we would have known that this existed during the week in between Christmas & New Years when we were fiending for Indian food. Now that we know, I have no doubt we will soon become regulars. nnWe have also tried Tamarind in Oakland, but that place just made my mouth go numb after it was all said and done (and left me with an unpleasant digestion experience). Overall, Taste of India at CMU has become one of our favorite spots for authentic Indian cuisine, and we highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and satisfying meal. You can taste the love cooked in.

I ordered the signature dish, and it arrived promptly, beautifully presented. The place was crowded, as usual, but the line went fairly quickly. On my way in, I saw a $5 fish sandwich with creamy coleslaw advertised outside. The flavors were exceptional—clear, fresh, and well-balanced. Looked and smelled delicious, so I paid inside with my groceries. I will definitely be coming back soon to try more of their menu items. They were really nice and asked me what kind of bread I wanted and what I wanted on the sandwich. nnSome lady that was "in a rush" was upset her sandwich wasn't ready when she came out (but they explained the fish was cooked, but they couldn't set up the sandwich without knowing what bread or toppings she wanted). Just watching the way they dealt with this customer was great for me. The guys were so friendly and patient. From the moment I walked in, I was greeted warmly by the staff, which immediately made me feel welcome. The coleslaw was also awesome! The drink selection was impressive, with a variety of options to suit different tastes. I am so happy I stopped by when I did.

we booked the aloft W down the street and those posers, actually sold our room out from under us and, as a 'sorry' comp'ed us a room at the Hilton here.. .. now, first off, if you're going to say sorry with a comp, why wouldn't it be a nice hotel. not that the hilton isn't 'nice' but it's not quite at the level of the aloft. The location made it easy to walk to several popular sights and shopping districts. Overall, the hotel provided excellent value for our money, combining comfort, convenience, and great service. nni hesitate to give this place only 3 stars because what else do you really expect from this place. One of the highlights was the rooftop terrace, offering stunning panoramic views and a perfect spot for drinks at sunset. service is good. room is BASIC. no frills. they have an iron so you can iron your wrinkled shirts before going off to your meetings in the morning. hair dryer works. hot water. room is quiet. If you're visiting this city, I highly recommend staying here. but oh well. We’ll definitely consider returning on our next visit. not a massive selection but there were 9 staff down there waiting on about 8 customers hand and foot. We dined at the on-site restaurant and enjoyed a delicious breakfast buffet with a variety of fresh options. The hotel also offered a nice fitness center that we used for a quick workout in the morning. We loved waking up to the view of the city skyline from our window. so it's good for what it is but not a ton more.

Goulash in the Contrucci household was made of elbow noodles, beef and spaghetti sauce. I guess you can't believe everything your parents tell you right? nnSo going in here, I was thinking, great.. . However, the overall taste did not live up to the description or my expectations. What was set in front me looked NOTHING like what I was used to. It was a mish mosh of veggies, noodles, gravy and some random unidentifiable food items. Growing up, her version was a simple, hearty stew with ground beef, elbow macaroni, and a tomato-based sauce. Unfortunately, what arrived was quite different from my childhood memories. The flavors seemed muted, and the sauce lacked the rich tomato tang I was craving. I know, I know, this is like "world famous" goulash, but I was NOT into it! On the plus side, the portion size was generous, and the presentation was appealing. I love it, and honestly, I feel like I never get the same version of it anywhere in the Burgh. This was a no frills version, with scallop sliced potatoes and a thick vinegar sauce. Maybe a bit too much, but not enough for me to eat it all! nnWould I go back? That said, if you're open to trying a different take on the dish, it might be worth a shot, especially if you enjoy experimenting with flavors. Oh well, on to the next one right?

Parking can be a challenge, especially during peak hours, so plan accordingly. The same goes for the food. Some dishes are awesome (shrimp and grits, stuffed chicken) while others I would definitely shy away from (pizza). If you are a beer lover, they have some good brews which are actually crafted on site. The beer can be better than the food more times than not and I would recommend people to go here for that more than the food. Prices are reasonable, which is a big plus, but I expect a bit more consistency for what I pay. If you give this place a shot, prepare to roll the dice because you don't know who you will get, or what the food will be like when it comes out. The one thing you will be guaranteed to have if you are so inclined is a nice brew made on-site. The ambiance is generally pleasant, but on busy nights it can get noisy and cramped.

We decided to give it a try since it was so conveniently located. The atmosphere was nice, and if I was rating only for atmosphere I'd give it 4 stars. However, I'm mainly rating their food and service. We were greeted promptly, but after that the service was spotty and it took awhile to receive our drinks/food even though there weren't many people in the dining room. Overall, Olive or Twist provided a delightful dining experience that I would highly recommend to anyone visiting Pittsburgh. We also appreciated the thoughtfully curated wine list, which had several options by the glass. In fact, I couldn't finish it. The meat tasted like old lunch meat and the bread was nothing more than a cheap, glorified hot dog roll that was soggy. Throughout the meal, the service was attentive without being intrusive, making us feel well cared for. nnOverall, if I was going back to Pittsburgh in this area, I would stay far away from Olive or Twist.

One of the standout features is the outdoor seating area, surrounded by greenery that adds to the quaint vibe. Whether you're meeting friends or seeking a peaceful spot to unwind, Cafe Zinho delivers on all fronts. My two friends were already there and then.. . there was just me in the restaurant, which scared me a little bit but I have to have faith in my fellow Yelpers. nnThe waitress was an adorable woman who was so friendly, helpful and enthusiastic about the dishes in a quiet manner. The ambiance of Cafe Zinho immediately makes you feel at home, with its warm lighting and charming decor. I look forward to returning soon to explore more of their menu and soak up the inviting ambiance once again. We ordered the goat cheese for an appetizer which was just so ooey and gooey deliciousness and then for the piece de resistance ordered the sea bass special that night which had capers, a potato, rice and some roasted vegetables. Great light combination and not too heavy. The size of the sea bass was like of the entire whole fish. To top it off we had the rice pudding dessert which was similar to flan but I thought this was so tasty. Their coffee is rich and expertly brewed, highlighting the flavors of the beans beautifully. nnnI am so glad I went to Cafe Zinho finally and would happily come back here again.

Would I go back.. . yes! The dessert selection was equally impressive, featuring decadent treats that satisfied every sweet tooth. By the end of the night, I felt both relaxed and invigorated by the experience. The menu offered a diverse selection of gourmet dishes, each presented beautifully on the plate. I especially enjoyed the chocolate fondant, which was warm and gooey in the center. n-  They serve drinks at the bar out front and also provide table service; BUT when the show starts, the table service stops. The accompanying wine pairing was expertly chosen to complement the meal. I happened upon this place for an elite event. The tables are pretty nice. I liked the raised platform area, but those chairs lacked arms that the ones on the floor had. I think I'd go with the raised bar tables on each side next time. n-  They bring around the checks after the show. If you don't want to wait forever, ask for the check early (before the show) or bring cash. nnFour stars instead of five because the will call staff was really rude. I won free tickets (plural) or so I thought. Guests mingled easily, sharing stories and laughter that filled the room with a sense of community. The staff greeted each guest with genuine smiles and attentive service, which made everyone feel special. I ended up having to buy another ticket, which was at a different table, because she wouldn't move my comped ticket. Lesson of the day.. . skip the will call window.

The menu also offers a variety of unique options, like their white pizza with garlic and spinach, which is simply divine. We can’t wait for our next visit to try more of their delicious offerings! Toss salad is good with the pizza and the Calzones are great too!! If you’re ever in Pittsburgh and craving pizza, this spot should be at the top of your list. Look at the specialty pizzas on the back of the menu cause that's where it's at!! Every time we visit, the aroma of freshly baked dough and melting cheese welcomes us in. They also have a great selection of craft beers that pair wonderfully with their pies. 10 old booths and lots of old sports memorabilia. It seriously hasn't been updated since the first time I've been here, 18 years ago. Don't expect an immaculately impressive bathroom, but you can find the only cloth roller towel I've EVER seen, straight from 1949.  nnIt's BYOB so bring some B or buy some from the store next door. nn (I don't really understand the previous reviewer's complaint about greasiness, I've never had this issue. But I probably would not buy a piece of cheesecake from here cause come on, it probably wasn't make fresh here and it it wasn't then what's the point of getting it?? )nnThis is always a good choice for pizza! !

We appreciated the knowledgeable and friendly staff who took the time to understand our needs and preferences. Each visit felt personalized, never rushed or pressured. Recently, we recommended Walter E Smith to several friends who were equally impressed by their experience. On one occasion, when we had an issue with a minor defect, customer service promptly addressed it without any hassle. The table he recommended is beautiful but does not at all stand up to what he said it would. This table is only 3 1/2 months old and already has wood chipping off, many many dents and looks absolutely horrible. This table is so softI can dent/scratch it with my fingernail. Delivery was always timely and professional, with the team handling everything carefully. After only 2 months use I called the store to tell them the sales clerk clearly did not know the product he was selling, if he did he never would have recommended this table. I was told they did not cover customer abuse and can't be held accountable for a sales person giving me bad information. It's the sylvan coffee table.. .. DO NOT BUY IT!! I dropped the remote control on it and it left a huge dent. The quality of the materials they used was evident in every piece we considered. I told them I would bring it in myself and they said no. My end tables and cocktail table are extremely durable/well made and are exactly what I wanted. I am disappointed the table I was most concerned about is horrible.

The Hornets’ defense looks stronger than ever, a key factor in winning close games. Okay, not so much on that last one. nnYou see, back during the days of the Revolutionary War, the English commander sent a letter back to London, referring to Charlotte as "a veritable hornet's nest of rebellion. " Early preseason games have shown flashes of brilliance, with players like Kemba Walker stepping up as leaders. While challenges remain, the Hornets are poised to make a significant impact in the Eastern Conference. The Time Warner Cable Arena is a nice, modern arena with the appropriate number of comfortable seats that have a good view of the court, plenty of sky boxes and lots of concessions that charge the usual arm and a leg. nnThe name seems to have helped some. The excitement in the city is palpable as fans eagerly anticipate the return of their beloved team. Yay? nnAs for the "Lady Cats" I referenced in my earlier review.. . they are now the "Honey Bees" and they're just as cheery now as they were then.

The music playlist is just right—not too loud, but enough to set a good mood. I especially recommend the appetizers—they’re perfect for sharing. nnToday was my third visit. Halfway through my taco salad, I felt a clump of hair in my mouth. I fished it out, and although I really wanted to believe it had just fallen off my sleeve or shoulder, the clump looked nothing like my hair (blond) or my companion's (red). Their signature cocktails are particularly good, and I appreciate the creative presentation. He picked up the glob of hair off the napkin and told us that it couldn't be the restaurant's fault because none of the employees have dark-brown hair. The staff is friendly and attentive, always making sure our needs are met without being overbearing. )nnThen he walked away, said something to the server that sounded like "wants a free meal. " I’ve noticed that during peak hours it can get quite busy, so reservations might be a good idea if you’re planning to visit with a larger group. nnGross as it was, I understand that mistakes happen. But when he implied that I was lying -- that pissed me off. If something similar had happened in my restaurant, I would have fallen all over myself trying to make it right, not insulted the customer. nnTotal lack of class and decency. I’ve recommended this spot to friends and colleagues, and they’ve all enjoyed it as much as I have.

nnChicken!! ! Best Ethiopian Meat Dish I have eaten so far! Spicy and FULL of Flavor! I would love to see more dessert options in the future to complement the savory dishes. ! ! Biggest difference must be the blend and volume of seasonings used!! ! nnMost Unique Timatim and Spiciest though my least favorite of all the ones I have eaten.. . I started with a cup of Ethiopian coffee, which was rich and aromatic, reminding me of the authentic coffee ceremonies I had experienced before. The communal style of eating with injera encourages sharing and adds to the overall experience. Overall, Red Sea has clearly put effort into maintaining its authenticity while improving customer experience. I was curious to see if Red Sea had improved or changed over the years. The traditional Ethiopian decor, with its vibrant colors and cultural artifacts, set the perfect tone for the meal. For the main course, I ordered the combination platter to get a taste of various dishes. I also tried the shiro, a chickpea stew, which was creamy and comforting. Compared to my previous visit, I felt the service was more polished and efficient. nnChicken Taquitos (from the freezer section of a Grocery store) Awful! Is this Tex-Mex on Ethiopian? This was the only part of the meal that was a Total Disappointment.. nnDishes are "Made to order" so it will take a little longer than you may expect if you are not used to eating at Very Good Ethiopian restaurants! Service is OK, do not expect the man to be overly friendly until he knows you, do not expect your order to be 100%! Their dessert menu is the perfect ending to any meal, with decadent options that are worth saving room for. I've ordered the cake batter, caramel apple, and s'mores and haven't been disappointed in any so far. The restaurant also maintains a clean and well-organized space, adding to the overall enjoyable experience. It is served cold in a martini glass with warm pita chips and is just amazing! The staff is incredibly friendly and attentive, always ready to recommend dishes or accommodate special requests. nnThe only thing that lacks sometimes is the service, especially on my last visit. The portion size was generous, leaving me satisfied but not overly full. I also tried a slice of their homemade pie, which was the perfect sweet ending to the meal. The salad was pretty much what you'd expect, and the Sizzling Sensation definitely perked up my taste buds. I usually love black pepper, but this was a little much for me. The vegetarian dishes aren't cheap, running around $12-15 for an entree, though the minimum order for delivery is $12. The moment I walked through the door, I was greeted by a warm and inviting atmosphere. Prices were reasonable, especially considering the quality of the food and service.

nnGradually, over the past year, the prices have continued to increase to the point of being dinner menu prices for lunch size meals. This place doesn't suck, but it's not very good. The only time you should really go is if it's your birthday so you can have free beer. Throughout the meal, the soothing background music and warm lighting created a welcoming vibe. ), a salad topped with locally made cheese curds (absolutely perfect, even for a shaky stomach) and hot, crispy wings (not half-price but so tasty I ordered seconds anyway). nnThe restaurant was slow so it was nice and quiet while my Advil settled in. It broke on my lunch hour so I went to AutoZone and bought one. I how long it would be to get to it and how long it would take. Not too impressed though, and won't be in my top 3 choices for the future. nnHere's my list: nPro's: nLocation nSelf-Park at the Greyhound Bus garage a block down the street (anywhere from $5-$13/day depending on weekday or weekend) nWalkable to all sporting venues nGreat restaurant across the street NOT associated with the hotel (Tonic) nFantastic gym and indoor pool nnCon's: nRack rate='spensive nSelf park at hotel is $20/day, ouch, w/ no in and out nRoom had a stink that didn't go away nMaids like to knock to clean the rooms starting at 8 AM, and do so multiple times if you don't put the privacy sign out nHotel staff not particularly nice as what you'd expect out of a Westin nThe Fish Market (restaurant in the hotel) super 'spensive w/o great snack offerings, and again, not so nice service nWalls are super thin- so much so that we had morning wakeup calls from our "neighbor" hitting the head, gross nBeing colocated with the convention center means lots of traffic around the hotel and lots of obnoxious people n~~~~~ nIs now when I mention that we got the place for $70/night on Priceline (4 star, you'll either get this or the Omni)? nnI'm not sure how big this airport is, but after taking a stroll throughout the whole facility, I saw that every terminal was bustling with people. The ambiance of Alexander's was cozy and inviting, with soft lighting and tasteful decor. It’s a perfect place for both casual dinners and special occasions. Background music played softly, adding to the relaxed atmosphere without being intrusive. For dessert, we chose the chocolate lava cake, which was rich and decadent, melting in our mouths. Portions are huge, mine was easily two meals. Italian bread or rolls (not warmed up) w/ butter balls comes with the meal and there is EVOO on the table. For dessert, we ordered the chocolate chip cannolli which came with two - we enjoyed them but it pricey for the size $7. Aside from the dessert, the meal was reasonably priced. nnService was consistent with other Yelpers' reviews - really, really friendly. I would definitely recommend this spot to friends and family looking for a great meal in a comfortable setting. Because there were no mushrooms in my dish, she was suppose to take it off our bill but forgot so ended up giving a cash credit. Also I ended up packaging my Bolognese home since I couldn't eat it all and she asked if we wanted the rolls too and wrapped my pasta in saran wrap for the trip home to prevent any sauce spillage which was a smart move since we had walked here. nnOne comment though would be on the decor. You walk in and the bar area somewhat has a modern feel but then once you go into the dining room it is like you are warped back into time. There is just a lot of visual stimulation - over the top - that just doesn't go together. The hostess greeted us warmly and seated us promptly near a window with a nice view of the street. We'll be skipping other Italian places in the area and will be back again.

One side is for beer and wine and the other is for liquor. Parking is plentiful, and the location right off the interstate makes it convenient for quick stops. I've seen Fat Tire, arguably the most popular craft beer next to Sam Adams, close to expiration. People tend to go here to get a lot of cheap beer for a party and not necessarily to find local or micro brews,  They recently installed a growler station which is decent, but doesn't compare to Grapevine's just a few miles down the interstate. Two of the four taps were from New Belgium, another one was from a different Coloroda based brewery, and the only Carolina one was Thomas Creek. I wanted some of that but the keg was spent. There are frequent sales and promotions, especially around holidays, so it's worth checking back regularly. The selection at Frugal MacDoogal's is impressive, with rows upon rows of beer, wine, and spirits to choose from. The actual growler bottles were cheap though at only $3. Most places charges between $10-20 for your first time purchase. nnYou will find the major beer you want in here, although you will really only save money if buying a lot of it. The overall atmosphere feels welcoming and unpretentious. I've also noticed they carry a good selection of mixers, snacks, and party supplies.

Ultimately, this visit left me questioning whether fame alone can sustain a dining establishment without the substance to back it up. As one other reviewer rightly pointed out, Sammy's seems to be famous for claiming to be famous. nn(Note: this is for a visit about ten months earlier - could've sworn I'd already written one. ) Despite the stylish setting, the emptiness was palpable, making the atmosphere oddly cold and uninviting. The sandwich itself was, well, mediocre at best. There was a decent amount of meat, but it was pretty average. The other ingredients were also.. . average - certainly nothing that would generate "fame" because of its flavor. nnService was the usual gruff, put-upon treatment I've come to expect from small businesses in da 'Burgh. If you're famous, why is there never anyone in your restaurant? I haven't been back. It was difficult to shake the feeling that the fame was more about the name on the door than the food or experience inside. When my food arrived, presentation was impeccable, each plate a visual masterpiece.

Normally, not an issue, especially since she gave them my phone number and instructions to leave the flowers with my apartment office if I wasn't at home. Unfortunately, she had them delivered on a Saturday when I was out of town. This unexpected find has made it much easier for my family to stay connected despite the distance. On Tuesday, I called the number from her confirmation email and spoke to an unpleasant "customer service" representative. Finally, I returned home on Tuesday to find the flowers sitting on the ground by my door, not at the apartment office.. . The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it a perfect spot to relax and enjoy a meal. One friend chose the same as me except the potato soup and a 1/2 of aturkey club, and the other friend chose a cheesy baked potato. The drinks menu included a nice selection of craft beers and artisanal cocktails, which added a fun touch to our lunch. 00. Really pretty good for 3 people needing a quick lunch.
